input: Formalize in Lean 4 with Mathlib a finite combinatorial lemma inspired by Erdos Problem 689 parity-first top layer. Let I, H, Rlarge, Rmedium be finite sets. Assume H and Rlarge are disjoint subsets of I. Assume every h in H needs one selected incidence into I and every r in Rlarge needs one selected incidence into I. Suppose each large element contributes capacity at most 1 into I, and each medium element contributes capacity at most c into I. Prove the necessary inequality |H| <= c * |Rmedium| when a valid assignment exists, because the |Rlarge| incidences consume all large capacity and cancel. You may state it abstractly with natural numbers: if |H| + |Rlarge| <= |Rlarge| + c*|Rmedium| then |H| <= c*|Rmedium|. Attempt a proof.
